messages:
emily: Quick question — we converted a contractor who was on GlobalHire into full-time Redwood on 2025-06-01. GlobalHire reports employee deferrals and employer contributions for AprMay. Can those contributions be moved into our Fidelity account and can we credit Apr/May service for 401(k) eligibility and vesting?

jason-hr: Short take: we can often accept a rollover of the employee deferrals. Employer match and service credit require plan admin/vendor confirmation and sometimes an internal policy decision re: recognizing EOR time as credited service.

ilana-benefits: Please confirm: 1) employee name + DOB + last 4 SSN; 2) exact GlobalHire plan name; 3) export of contributions by paycheck date and type (pre-tax vs Roth); 4) any employer match detail. We'll open a transfer request with Fidelity once we have docs.

ben-payroll: Vendor note: Fidelity usually accepts incoming rollovers; retro employer contributions are allowed only if plan doc permits and vendor cutoff isn't passed (varies by provider). If retro match is allowed, payroll can process an off-cycle employer contribution but need approval from benefits and accounting for tax reporting.

emily: Got it. Employee is Trevor L (trevor.l@redwood.com). GlobalHire sent a CSV but it only labels one column "employer" without match% details. They also show contributions coded as "pre-tax". How do we verify match amounts?

ilana-benefits: Ask GlobalHire for a detailed contribution ledger that includes: pay period end, employee deferral amount (pretax/roth split), employer contribution amount and type, and date funds were remitted to their provider. Also ask for plan match formula and vesting schedule.

emily: Sending that now. Also, Trevor is worried about his 2025 annual deferral limit since he already hit $12k via GlobalHire payroll before conversion. He's planning catch-up; he's 50+ in 2025. How do rollovers vs deferrals interact with limit/catch-up?
jason-hr: Employee deferrals withheld by GlobalHire count toward the 2025 elective deferral limit for the calendar year if they were salary deferrals. Rollovers of those amounts into Fidelity do not create additional deferral counts. Catch-up contributions are separate and allowed if under limits and age-50+; but we need to reconcile amounts to avoid exceeding IRS limits. Benefits will reconcile once we get the CSV.

ben-payroll: Practical note: if we accept employee deferrals as a rollover, we must ensure double-withholding doesn't happen — payroll should not also treat those amounts as deferrals. We'll coordinate with Trevor to confirm year-to-date deferrals shown in Fidelity after rollover.

globalhire-bot: Automated notice: Contribution report attached for Trevor L (file: GH_TrevorL_2025-APR-MAY.csv). Plan: GlobalHire Collective 401k. Contact: planadmin@globalhire.com

ilana-benefits: Thanks @globalhire-bot. I'll open a case with Fidelity and ask whether the GlobalHire plan records are sufficient for a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer and whether service can be credited for vesting. Expect vendor response in ~7-10 business days.

emily: If Fidelity denies backdating service for vesting, is there any internal policy fallback?
jason-hr: If vendor denies, we can (1) accept the rollover of employee funds without match, and (2) consider a discretionary one-time employer contribution at our policy team's discretion, but that has accounting/tax implications and usually requires exec sign-off. We'll escalate if needed.

trevor-manager: Quick ask from manager POV: if service isn't credited, Trevor is still eligible for other benefits now that he's on Redwood payroll, right? (medical/HSA start dates were different).
ilana-benefits: Yes medical/HSA/FSA eligibility follows our standard benefits effective date for direct hires. 401(k) eligibility and vesting are governed by plan rules and any recognized credited service. We'll keep you posted.

emily: Thanks all. I'll follow up with GlobalHire for the detailed ledger and post back.
